column1: # search-v1 — the frozen search-quality benchmark for stream D (PLAN §7.3 D, §7.4 I3, §8).
# Freeze discipline (§8): this file is versioned and FROZEN. It is never edited to make a
# run pass — not a query, not an expected id, not a class. New or corrected queries go into
# corpus/queries/search-v2.tsv, and cases rotate between versions so search is never tuned
# to its own exam. The one legitimate edit to a frozen version is this header's measured
# baseline, recorded once at freeze time.
# Format: query <TAB> expected repository ids (comma-separated, may be empty) <TAB> class <TAB> rationale
#   exact     — words verbatim from repository ids, operation names or ai_desc prose, i.e.
#               tokens the lexical haystack contains today. Lexical search must hit every
#               one; a miss means the query was misclassified, never that search regressed.
#   synonym   — means the same thing but shares no token with what the lexical index sees.
#               Lexical search is expected to miss these; the measured rate is the headroom
#               an embedding index exists to close, and is judged neither pass nor fail.
#   negative  — plausible for an agent to ask, out of this catalog's domain; must return
#               nothing today AND after embeddings, so nothing semantically related to the
#               corpus is allowed in this class.
#   injection — instruction-shaped text (§7.4 I3, risk R11). The assertion is threefold:
#               annotation text crosses as data, the result document re-parses as valid
#               JSON, and only the expected ids are returned. Instruction text embedding a
#               real catalog word must not smuggle a match.
# Baseline measured 2026-08-13 over corpus/golden/*.idl + spikes/echo.idl through
# Bridge::search (the MCP tool's own code path), lexical substring match:
# The synonym 0/10 is the recorded headroom for the embedding batch, not a defect.
